Author: T. Vinod Kumar
Bench: T. Vinod Kumar
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice T. Vinod Kumar
 Writ Petition No.17407 of 2024
Order:

Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for respondent Nos.1, 3 and 5, learned Government Pleader for Municipal Administration and Urban Development appearing for respondent No.2, and Sri B.Jagan Madhav Rao, learned Standing Counsel, appearing for respondent No.4, and perused the record.
2. Shorn of unnecessary details, the case of the petitioner, in brief, is that his land admeasuring 275 square yards situated at Gollaguda Area, Nalgonda District, was acquired by the authorities, in the year 1997, for the purpose of formation of 60 feet wide road, without initiating any proceedings under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short, 'the Act of 1894') and without paying any compensation.
3. Petitioner contends that aggrieved by the inaction of respondents, he had approached the Lokayuktha, Hyderabad, and on the direction of the said Lokayuktha, the respondents-authorities have filed their report in 24.01.2024, wherein they have stated as under:
"Hence, I submit that the payment of compensation to the Complainant Sri Md.Nazeeruddin is in progress and in these above said circumstances, I request the Hon'ble Registrar of Lokayuktha to kindly provide 04 months of time to obtain the exemption orders from the Government from application of provisions of Chapter Ii & III of RFCTLA & RR Act-2013 and for payment of compensation duly submitting the fresh requisition proposals to the District Collector."
4. Petitioner further contends that the respondents despite making the aforementioned statement before the Hon'ble Lokayuktha did not initiate the proceedings nor paid the compensation to petitioner compelling him to file the present Writ Petition.
5.

This Court, on 18.10.2024, at the pre-admission stage of writ petition, by considering the fact that the petitioner was dispossessed in the year 1997 without initiating any proceedings for acquiring his land under the Act of 1894 and also taking note of the fact that the authorities have indicated before the Lokayuktha that within four months, they would obtain exemption orders from the Government from application of provisions of Chapter II and III of the Act 30 of 2013 and having failed to adhere Md. sentences.text: When the matter is taken up for hearing, on 24.10.2024, the 3rd respondent, who had appeared before this Court along respondent Nos.4 and 5, had informed that the Government had granted exemption from application of provisions of Chapter II and III of the Act 30 of 2013 for payment of compensation and that the compensation amount would be paid to the petitioner by initiating necessary action.

6. Today, when the matter is taken up for further hearing, learned Standing Counsel appearing on behalf of the 4th respondent submitted that the required probable sum of Rs.1,20,18,220/- for initiating land acquisition proceedings in respect of the petitioner's property had been deposited with the 5th respondent in its entirety, with the last of the deposit being dt.25.10.2024.

7. Learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing on behalf of the 5th respondent submits that immediately on the deposit of the probable amount for initiating land acquisition proceedings, the said authority has sent declaration proposal under Section 19 of the Act 30 of 2013 to the District Collector for approval and caused publication of the same in the gazette vide Gazette No.68 dt.04.11.2024.

8. Learned Government Pleader would further submit that Gazette notification and notice under Section 21 of the Act 30 of 2013, was published in a conspicuous place on 06.11.2024 and 07.11.2024 and the same has also been served on the petitioner/ land loser.

9. Learned Government Pleader, by placing a copy of the written instructions as furnished to him by the 5th respondent dt.07.11.2024, would submit that after completion of statutory period as per notice issued under Section 21 of the Act 30 of 2013, the authorities would pass the award and pay the compensation to the land loser.

10. Learned Government Pleader thus submits that since the 5th respondent has already received the amount in respect of the compensation to be paid to the land loser and the authorities having initiated necessary action under the Act 30 of 2013, the authorities would complete the remaining exercise of passing award and paying the compensation within the time prescribed under the Act.
11.

Having regard to the submissions made as above, and taking note of the fact that the 4th respondent authority has now deposited the required probable amount of compensation to be paid for acquiring the land of the petitioner and the 5th respondent having initiated process of acquisition, this Court is of the view that the respondents-authorities are to be directed to complete the aforesaid process of acquisition and payment of compensation to the petitioner in respect of his land from which he was dispossessed in the year 1997, within the time frame prescribed under the Act 30 of 2013.
12. Subject to above direction, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
